title: Bounded-below coproduct continuity of internal Hom from stratified perfect sources
statement: Let T be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let d be an adic coefficient datum over a commutative ring A and R=A_T its completed ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let K be a bounded-above object of the ordinary derived category of R-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and assume IsIntegralStratifiedPerfect(T,d,K): there is a finite locally closed immersed stratification such that on a pro-etale cover of each stratum, K is isomorphic to the restriction of R tensor a bounded finite-projective A-complex [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For every small family M_i with a common integer cohomological lower bound N [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], the functor Rℋom_R(K,-) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] preserves the coproduct of this family, in the uncompleted derived category of R-module sheaves itself. Sizes are as in [def-weil-size-convention]. The coefficient datum is arbitrary and no rational algebra, finite-dimensionality or finite Krull-dimension assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(2)–(4) and final devissage, applied as in Lemma 6.8.12

proof.text: For a qcqs scheme S, a commutative ring sheaf R with A scalar action, and a source B bounded above by b, define C_S(B) to mean global Hom continuity on every qcqs pro-etale slice for families with an arbitrary common lower bound N. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-internal-hom-lower-bound], internal Hom H(B,M) has lower bound N-b. Restriction is exact; [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identify restriction of H with H on the slice. For a weakly etale object W→S, the site equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies W_proet with S_proet/W. Transport the restricted ring, its modules and all A actions along this equivalence using [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No constant-ring identification is made.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(3),(4), details of the boundedness and restriction argument

proof.text: Here is the locality argument for C_S, including the distinction between internal and global Hom. For any uniformly bounded-below family M_i, form α:⊕_i H(B,M_i)→H(B,⊕_i M_i). Its source and target have the common lower bound N-b from step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-derived-sections-bounded-below-coproducts], RΓ(W,α) is exactly the global Hom comparison for the restricted family on every qcqs W. Conversely, if these comparisons are isomorphisms on every qcqs W, the cone of α is zero: test on affine weakly contractible W, where exact evaluation identifies derived evaluation with evaluation on complexes; its cohomology sections all vanish. Such W cover every object, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover] applied to affine objects, so every cohomology sheaf of the cone is zero. Slice restriction of α is its corresponding comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; restriction also commutes with sums (the sheafified sectionwise description in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]). Thus C_S(B) can be checked on a pro-etale covering by qcqs objects V_a: for any qcqs W, the objects W×_S V_a cover W, all their further qcqs slices are allowed in C_{V_a}, and the preceding cone test shows α|_{V_a}=0 on cones, hence α is an isomorphism on W. The qcqs fibre products and covering operations are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. The bound b is fixed before this test, so no unbounded totalization is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(3),(4), proof of pro-etale locality for bounded-above sources

proof.text: The class C_S is closed under shifts, finite sums, direct summands and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles of bounded-above objects. Indeed H sends source triangles to triangles and respects shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; the comparisons α form a morphism of triangles. Direct sums of these triangles are triangles, as seen on their mapping-cone complexes using [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. In the long exact cohomology sequences, if the comparisons for two vertices are isomorphisms, exactness gives it for the third; a comparison on a direct summand is the corresponding direct summand of the comparison. The unit R belongs to C_S because RHom_R(R,M)=RΓ(S,M), and the same identity holds on every slice, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-derived-sections-bounded-below-coproducts] applies. Consequently R⊗_A^L P belongs to C_S for every bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules: each projective term is a summand of a finite free module, and the finite sequence of stupid-truncation triangles builds P from these terms. All operations are finite; no compact-generation assertion is being used.

If j:U→S is a quasi-compact open immersion, then j_! carries C_U to C_S. The exact adjunction j_!⊣j^{-1} is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. It induces a derived adjunction: restriction sends K-injectives to K-injectives, since maps into a restricted K-injective from an acyclic complex are adjoint to maps from its acyclic exact j_!-image. Apply the chain adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to obtain Hom_D(j_!B,M[r])=Hom_D(B,j^{-1}M[r]) for every r. By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and shift compatibility from step 1, these are the cohomology groups of the global derived Homs. The bijections are natural in M and hence intertwine the canonical coproduct comparisons. Since coproducts of A-modules are exact, the property C_U(B) implies that the comparison on S is an isomorphism on every cohomology group, and thus an isomorphism in D(A). Restriction is exact and preserves coproducts by its sectionwise restriction and sheafification description, so the common lower bound on M_i remains the same on U. The argument applies on every qcqs slice W, with U_W=U×_S W; this is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], and restriction of j_! is the extension by zero for U_W, directly from its presheaf definition in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. This proves the required comparison on every W.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14(2), specialized to the quasi-compact open immersions needed here

proof.text: Let i:Z→S be closed with quasi-compact open complement h:V→S, and suppose L on Z is locally R_Z⊗_A^L P with P a bounded finite-projective A-complex. Assume L is bounded above. We prove C_S(i_*L). Throughout, for a weakly etale site object W→S with Z_W=Z×_S W and i_W:Z_W→W, [lem-exc-closed-localization] (the cartesian square of W→S and i) gives (i_*F)|_W≅i_{W,*}(F|_{Z_W}) and identifies the two composite inverse images (i^{-1}F)|_{Z_W}≅i_W^{-1}(F|_W); applied to the ring sheaf R this identifies R_Z|_{Z_W} with i_W^{-1}(R|_W), so the hypothesis on L and the conclusion restrict to W with the same kind of coefficients. By step 2 we can first replace S by an affine open S'; the complement of Z∩S' in S' is V∩S', quasi-compact since V→S is quasi-compact (V is quasi-compact and S quasi-separated). Refine a trivializing cover of Z by a finite cover of affine ind-etale objects Z_a→Z, using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. The lift v of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties] gives affine pro-etale S_a=v(Z_a)→S with S_a×_S Z=Z_a. Together with V these S_a cover S: they cover every point of Z and V covers its complement. They are a finite family of qcqs objects. On V, i_*L is zero. On S_a it is i_{a,*}(R_{Z_a}⊗_A^L P_a), with i_a:Z_a→S_a and R_{Z_a}=R_Z|_{Z_a}. This base-change identity is the restriction isomorphism of [lem-exc-closed-localization] for W=S_a (on sections it is (i_*F)(W)=F(W×_S Z) of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]); both closed pushforwards are exact because the complements are quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], so it holds termwise on representing complexes. Put P_{S_a}=R_{S_a}⊗_A P_a, with R_{S_a}=R|_{S_a}, and h_a:S_a\Z_a→S_a. By the inverse-image identification above, R_{Z_a}≅i_a^{-1}R_{S_a}, and exact inverse image commutes with tensoring by each finite projective term (a retract of a finite free module), so i_a^{-1}P_{S_a}=P_{S_a}|_{Z_a}≅R_{Z_a}⊗_A P_a. The localization short exact sequences of the same open-closed node, applied termwise, give the triangle h_{a,!}(P_{S_a}|_{S_a\Z_a})→P_{S_a}→i_{a,*}(P_{S_a}|_{Z_a}). Steps 3 and 4 put its first two vertices in C_{S_a}, so its third is in C_{S_a}. Step 3 now proves C_S(i_*L). Notice that the trivializing cover was lifted from Z to ambient site objects; no assertion that internal Hom commutes with arbitrary closed inverse image is made.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14, final paragraph: lifting a trivializing cover of a closed stratum and the triangle h_!M→M→K

proof.text: The hypothesis gives a finite stratification with perfect local models, and the upper bound b is supplied separately. Refine this finite stratification to a finite filtration by closed subsets with locally perfect layers. Explicitly, express each stratum as an open intersected with a closed subset and list the finitely many opens involved (including complements of those closed subsets). The subset F_k of points belonging to at most k of these opens is closed: its complement is the union of the intersections of k+1 opens. On F_k\F_{k-1} the membership patterns form a finite clopen partition, each piece lying in one original stratum. Thus the restriction of K to every layer is locally perfect. If m is the number of listed opens, set F_{-1}=∅ and |F_m|=|T|; give every F_k for 0≤k≤m its reduced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Thus F_m is T_red, while its open complement is empty. Each membership-pattern piece of a layer maps to its original stratum: the piece is open in the reduced scheme F_k\F_{k-1}, hence reduced; the stratum's immersion is a closed immersion into an open W of T containing the stratum, the piece lies in W, and its image lies in that of the closed immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives the factorization of the piece through the stratum scheme over T. Exact inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] carries a local finite-projective tensor description to its pullback: each finite-projective term is a retract of a finite free module, so pulling back its splitting gives the same tensor description with the pulled-back ring. Thus the locally perfect assertion survives this scheme-theoretic refinement, using inverse-image coefficients throughout. Every complement used is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], since T is noetherian; the same applies to its intersections with affine opens, so the complementary open immersions are quasi-compact morphisms. In any qcqs pro-etale base change these complements remain quasi-compact, so all preceding steps remain applicable there.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 via Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); finite stratification refinement for the devissage in Lemma 6.3.14

proof.text: The source K already satisfies the finite stratified-perfect predicate; no integral characterization is needed here. Put U_k=T\F_k for -1≤k≤m, so U_{-1}=T and U_m=∅. Let j_k:U_k→T be the open immersion and L_k=j_{k,!}(K|_{U_k}). For each 0≤k≤m, the layer Y_k=F_k\F_{k-1} is closed in U_{k-1}; write i_k:Y_k→U_{k-1} and h_k:U_k→U_{k-1}. Its open complement is quasi-compact. Apply the localization short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] termwise to K|_{U_{k-1}}, then apply the exact functor j_{k-1,!}. This gives a triangle L_k→L_{k-1}→j_{k-1,!}i_{k,*}(K|_{Y_k}). The identification of its first vertex uses the adjunctions of the same open-closed node: for module sheaves F on U_k and G on T, Hom(j_{k-1,!}h_{k,!}F,G)=Hom(h_{k,!}F,j_{k-1}^{-1}G)=Hom(F,h_k^{-1}j_{k-1}^{-1}G)=Hom(F,j_k^{-1}G). Thus j_{k-1,!}h_{k,!} and j_{k,!} are canonically isomorphic as left adjoints to j_k^{-1}. This natural identification respects the counits, and exactness permits applying it termwise to complexes. The inverse-image restrictions compose, with coefficients always the inverse image of A_T. By step 6, K|_{Y_k} is locally perfect and bounded above. Step 6 puts i_{k,*}(K|_{Y_k}) in C_{U_{k-1}}, and step 4 puts the third vertex in C_T. Start with L_m=0, which lies in C_T by the definition, and descend in k using step 3 and these triangles to obtain L_{-1}=K in C_T. This uses localization only on the complementary opens, and requires no closed inverse-image base-change identity.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14, reduction to a locally closed stratum and its open-closed factorization; applied as instructed by Lemma 6.8.12

proof.text: The local comparison argument above shows that the canonical internal-Hom coproduct comparison is an isomorphism. Equivalently, internal Hom sends every colimit cofan of the supplied family to a colimit cofan, which is PreservesColimit of its discrete diagram. This is a sheaf-valued assertion before global sections; no global-Hom conclusion is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem integralStratifiedPerfect_internalHom_preservesColimit
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T]
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules T (pbcAdicCompletion T d)))
    (b : ℤ) [K.IsLE b] (hK : IsIntegralStratifiedPerfect T d K)
    (I : Type (u + 1)) (M : I → DerivedCategory
      (pbcModules T (pbcAdicCompletion T d)))
    (N : ℤ) (hM : ∀ i, (M i).IsGE N) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor M)
      ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
        (ProEt.topology T) (pbcAdicCompletion T d))).obj (op K))
